A1.justification: Both complete 20-page PDFs describe PrivacyRestore and include readable text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–D. Pages 2–20 match in extracted text and rendered appearance; differences are confined to the first-page author block and version stamp.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original medical-diagnosis, privacy-attack, ablation and inference-efficiency results on Pri-Ddxplus and Pri-NLICE.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D retain these original empirical results, including evaluations across three LLM backbones.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same attention-head selection, ORPO restoration-vector training, attention-aware weighted aggregation, noise injection and inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same medical-diagnosis datasets, Pri-Ddxplus and Pri-NLICE, with identical privacy-level scenarios and prompt-injection and attribute-inference attacks.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 5 and 6 retain the same comparators: No Protection, Direct Removal, DP and DP on Privacy Spans. The component-ablation comparators also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices A, C and D report identical dataset splits, preprocessing, model backbones, privacy thresholds, metrics, training settings and decoding procedures.

E4.justification: The same ablations test attention-head selection, restoration-vector training and aggregation in Tables 1, 5 and 6. Privacy-attack analyses and supplementary examples are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and reported findings are identical, including performance and privacy results in Tables 1, 5 and 6, efficiency results in Tables 2, 7 and 8, and dataset statistics.

T1.justification: The privacy-span assumptions, threat model, Equations (1)–(10), and Appendix B's combinatorial argument about reconstructing privacy spans are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about PrivacyRestore, attention-aware aggregation, privacy protection, utility and inference efficiency.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and attack-defense explanations are identical. Both retain the same limitations concerning healthcare-only evaluation, evolving privacy vocabularies, retraining and out-of-vocabulary spans.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains identical implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware descriptions and training-time information. Reported access information and embedded external-link destinations also match.

R1.justification: Section 2, the bibliography and the positioning relative to differential privacy, secure multiparty computation and activation steering are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds Junyao Yang to the author list, changes 'ZhengdongLu' to 'Zhengdong Lu', and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific prose and document organization are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: The first-page author block becomes wider and its alignment shifts to accommodate the added author. Figures, tables, captions, equations and all subsequent page layouts remain identical.

improvement.justification: v2 changes author attribution and first-page presentation while retaining identical scientific content and evidence throughout the main text and appendices. These limited edits do not meaningfully alter the paper's overall quality.
